exposure: mode of delivery (elective cesarean vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery)
cohort: 1329 deliveries (584 elective cesarean and 745 spontaneous vaginal delivery) at a tertiary hospital in South India over 2 years.
finding: Neonatal respiratory morbidity and need for respiratory support were significantly higher in the elective cesarean group compared to the spontaneous vaginal delivery group overall.
mod_finding: Comparing early-term elective cesarean deliveries (37+0-38+6 weeks) to term elective cesarean deliveries (>=39 weeks) showed only a modest, non-significant increase in neonatal respiratory morbidity and need for respiratory support.
